output.methodChoice: Read the initial evidence, then collected X5 (27 Apr–1 Nov weekly rates with ops-review notes) to test whether the week of 26 Oct was unusual. Stopped at one item; the rest of the scoring relies on the initial evidence.
output.brief: The rise in ratequote's 5xx rate is most likely ordinary week-to-week variation, not a fault from v4.18 or the replica move. The week of 26 Oct was 0.41%, while the service's normal upper band over the previous 26 weeks is 0.48% (X5). Under the team's own policy (E5), that week does not count as an incident, and the burn rate was 0.82x, below the 2x paging line. Booking completion was flat (E6), and the dashboard query and a manual recount agree (E2). The v4.18 rollout comparison (E3) is confounded because newly started pods can err more, so it does not show the release caused the rise. I have not tested the replica, partner-sync or per-pod explanations, so my confidence is moderate. Next steps: record the week at ops review, make no rollback, and do not mute alerting. Keep the standard weekly check, and if the next week is also high, open an incident and check the pod-level data.
